label: copy-phase input token i
explanation: Fires only during the copy phase, on steps where the fed-back input token is the letter i (i.e. the model just emitted i and is now emitting the token after it). All activation mass is on in_tok == i; it never fires in the original phase, on <DEL>, or on any other input token. About 75% of copy-phase i inputs activate. Activations at recall_idx 1 (i was the first original token) are weak and account for only ~3% of mass; adding recall_idx >= 2 raises dev F1 from 0.85 to 0.885. The strongest activations come from sequences with an i i doublet or an i deep into the sequence, but the false positives (inactive copy-phase i) do not follow an obvious pattern.

issues: The core claims hold. On the dev split, phase share is original 0, delimiter 0, copy 1.000, and in_tok == i carries 100% of activation mass. The original predicate has 0 missed activations on test. Test precision is 0.744 (about 75% of copy-phase i inputs fire), recall 1.0, F1 0.853.
The recall_idx == 1 claim is right: on dev, recall_idx 1 carries 3.2% of mass and fires at about 38% of i inputs there, against about 85% at recall_idx >= 2.

The claim that the false positives show no obvious pattern is wrong. The recall_idx == 1 case (i was the first original token) is a systematic false-positive class. It accounts for about half of all test false positives: they fall from 23325 to 11507 when recall_idx >= 2 is added, and test precision rises from 0.744 to 0.845. The test misses listing shows this directly, with 4 of 8 shown false positives at recall_idx 1 (e.g. 'i w l <DEL> *i* w', 'i 3 w s <DEL> *i* 3 w').

The remaining false positives depend on the preceding token: dev precision for recall_idx >= 2 is e 0.55, t 0.62, u 0.66, against l 0.99, r 0.98, a 0.97. This is a graded effect, not a clean class. Excluding e/t/u lowers test F1 to 0.866, so the simpler predicate is still better.

The author found the better predicate (dev F1 0.885) but kept the worse one, so the reported predicate leaves a known systematic false-positive class in place. With recall_idx >= 2, test F1 is 0.885 and mass recall 0.968.

Minor: when i comes right after another i, the second i in the copy phase (the doublet) is often weaker than the first (e.g. 0.95 then 0.71, or 0.90 then 0.28). The top activations come from the first i of a doublet, and from mid-to-late positions in the sequence.
